Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo - RTBF / Deletion workflow follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today  really helpful to understand your flow and compliance needs. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can scope the work and timing: 

- Scope observed: user-generated content (transactions, chat prompts), user profile PII (email, name, account id).
- Required actions: support per-user deletion (RTBF) that removes PII from active indexes and serving caches; provide an auditable confirmation; address backups/residual copies and data residency constraints (US-only).
- Desire: deletion-to-confirmation SLA of ~7 days, ideally faster for primary store.

Open questions for us to confirm (will loop in engineering/legal):
1) Do you require deletion from backups (cold backups) within the same SLA or is "logical deletion + retention window for backups" acceptable?
2) Any specific regulatory hold requirements (e.g., subpoena, retention windows) for subset of users?
3) Are there specific log types you need preserved for fraud/security that should be excluded from standard RTBF?

Next steps:
- I'll loop in our engineering and legal folks with the details and ask for a target timeline for purge + backup handling.
- Can we schedule a 30m technical sync this week to walk through your data flows and backup cadence? Please propose a couple of times.

Attaching a short RTBF process overview for context (high level).

Thanks 
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila  that recap is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For our security/compliance team, we need a clear statement on backups: we prefer that deleted user data is purged from backups within 30 days where technically possible. If there are technical/legal constraints that force longer windows, we need documented exceptions.
- Data residency: all production data (including backups) must remain in the US.
- Logs: we can tolerate anonymized logs for fraud detection, but any log that contains PII must be purged or redacted.

We can do a technical sync Thursday 10:00am PT or Friday 2:00pm PT  whichever works for your engineers.

Alex
Head of Engineering, FintechCo

Subject: Re: FintechCo - RTBF / Deletion workflow follow-up

Hi all  quick technical note ahead of the sync. Thanks for the clear asks, Alex. High-level constraints from the Redwood inference stack: 

- Active stores (indexes, user profile DBs, KV caches): we can support targeted per-user deletion and return an auditable deletion record within 24-72 hours depending on queueing and batch sizes.
- Serving caches & KV cache: we purge keys on delete requests; for in-flight cache copies it can take minutes-hours to fully expire depending on TTLs; we can accelerate for prioritized deletes.
- Backups: cold backups are typically stored as periodic snapshots (daily/weekly). Purging from immutable snapshot archives is non-trivial  typical options are: 
  a) Logical deletion + withholding restores for deleted IDs (fast)
  b) Replay rebuilds where we rehydrate stores without the deleted data (time & cost intensive)
  c) Expedited retention/exception: schedule snapshot overwrite within a retention window (e.g., 30 days) where snapshots are rotated and older snapshots are truncated.

Given standard snapshot cadence, a 30-day purge-from-backups commitment is feasible operationally if we coordinate retention windows and classify FTCH as us-only region. However, we should document any edge cases (e.g., disaster recovery snapshots stored in cold archive with longer retention).

Action items for sync:
- Confirm snapshot cadence for FintechCo (daily/weekly) and which archives are in scope.
- Agree on deletion SLA tiers (standard 30 days vs expedited 7 days for high-risk users).
- Identify logs that must be redacted vs preserved for fraud detection and the anonymization approach.

I'll attach our high-level RTBF process and a short technical appendix for the sync.

Thanks 
Dev Patel
Senior Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: RTBF-Process.pdf

- Contract language: we can commit to a documented RTBF process that covers active store deletion within 7 days and a backup purge objective of 30 days where feasible. We will include exceptions for legal hold and disaster recovery snapshots stored in long-term cold archives  those will be documented as exceptions and require separate handling.
- Residency: we confirm we can scope FintechCo to US-only regions and controls; we'll include this as a contractual data locale requirement.
- Auditability: we will provide deletion confirmation records and a runbook describing how deletion events propagate through caches, indexes, backups, and logs.

Next steps:
1) Camila  please confirm the sync time (Thu 10:00am PT).
2) Dev / Engineering  prepare a short appendix on snapshot cadence and which archives would be affected; outline steps to provide a 30-day backup purge objective and what the operational exceptions look like.
3) I'll draft a short addendum to our T&Cs reflecting the RTBF commitment + exceptions for review.

Happy to join the sync.

Best 
Laura Bennett
